investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HIV.front: What does a 4th-generation HIV immunoassay detect, and why does this matter?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HIV.back: It detects both p24 antigen and anti-HIV antibodies. Because p24 antigen appears before antibodies, the combined assay shortens the window period to about 4 weeks.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HIV.front: After a possible HIV exposure, when is a negative 4th-generation test considered reliable?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HIV.back: At 45 days (about 6–7 weeks) after the exposure. A negative 4th-gen assay at this point reliably excludes HIV for that exposure.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HIV.front: What CD4 count defines AIDS-level immune risk, and what prophylaxis is indicated?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HIV.back: CD4 <200 cells/mm3. This is the AIDS-defining threshold with high opportunistic-infection risk; start prophylaxis such as co-trimoxazole for PCP.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HIV.front: What does an undetectable viral load on ART signify?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HIV.back: Effective treatment. It reflects the principle Undetectable = Untransmittable (U=U): the virus cannot be sexually transmitted.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HIV.front: What is the time window for post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP/PEPSE) after a significant HIV exposure?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HIV.back: Within 72 hours of the exposure, started as soon as possible and never delayed.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HIV.front: What is the key action once HIV is confirmed on the supplementary assay?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HIV.back: Refer to specialist HIV care and start antiretroviral therapy (ART) promptly at diagnosis, regardless of CD4 count (universal ART), aiming for an undetectable viral load. Add opportunistic-infection prophylaxis (e.g. co-trimoxazole) if CD4 <200.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__STI.front: What is the first-line test for chlamydia and gonorrhoea?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__STI.back: Nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT), which amplifies pathogen DNA/RNA and is far more sensitive than culture.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__STI.front: Most sensitive genital specimen for chlamydia NAAT in women?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__STI.back: A self-taken vulvovaginal swab — more sensitive than first-void urine. In men, first-void urine is used.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__STI.front: When must extragenital (pharyngeal and rectal) NAAT swabs be taken?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__STI.back: Whenever there has been oral or anal sexual exposure (e.g. MSM). Genital-only testing misses extragenital infection.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__STI.front: Why take a culture after a positive gonorrhoea NAAT?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__STI.back: NAAT gives no sensitivity data. Culture before treatment tests antibiotic sensitivities, which matters given rising antimicrobial resistance.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__STI.front: Which organism should be tested for in persistent non-gonococcal urethritis/cervicitis, and what caveat applies?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__STI.back: Mycoplasma genitalium — test with macrolide-resistance markers and do not treat blindly with azithromycin because of widespread macrolide resistance.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__STI.front: What is the first-line treatment for a positive chlamydia NAAT, and what else must happen?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__STI.back: Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days (first-line, having displaced azithromycin; azithromycin if doxycycline is contraindicated or in pregnancy). Arrange partner notification.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__STI.front: After a positive gonorrhoea NAAT and culture, what is the treatment?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__STI.back: IM ceftriaxone (single dose) — a culture for sensitivities is always taken first because of rising antimicrobial resistance. Arrange partner notification and a test of cure.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Gon.front: Why must a gonorrhoea culture be taken BEFORE antibiotics are given?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Gon.back: Antibiotics kill the organism so it will not grow, and because N. gonorrhoeae has escalating antimicrobial resistance the culture is needed to obtain sensitivities that guide effective treatment.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Gon.front: What type of swab is used to sample for gonorrhoea culture and why?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Gon.back: A charcoal (Amies) transport swab. The charcoal neutralises toxic substances and preserves the fastidious, fragile gonococcus during transport to the lab.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Gon.front: Why can a NAAT not replace culture in gonorrhoea?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Gon.back: NAAT detects gonococcal DNA and confirms infection but cannot provide antibiotic sensitivities; culture of the live organism is required to guide therapy against a resistant organism.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Gon.front: What is the current first-line treatment for gonorrhoea?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Gon.back: A single intramuscular dose of ceftriaxone 1 g, tailored to culture sensitivities, followed by a test of cure.

• Disseminated gonococcal infection (arthritis, tenosynovitis, pustular rash)
  • and gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum in the newborn.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Gon.front: If the gonorrhoea culture is negative but the NAAT is positive, what do you do?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Gon.back: Still treat for gonorrhoea. Culture is less sensitive than NAAT (particularly at pharyngeal and rectal sites and if the swab was delayed/dry), so a negative culture does not exclude infection when the NAAT is positive.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Ure.front: What do polymorphonuclear leucocytes (PMNs) on a urethral Gram smear indicate?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Ure.back: Urethritis (urethral inflammation). The conventional cut-off is ≥5 PMNs per high-power field on a urethral smear (some criteria use ≥2).

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Ure.front: What microscopic finding gives a presumptive diagnosis of gonorrhoea on a urethral smear?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Ure.back: Gram-negative intracellular diplococci (kidney-bean-shaped organisms seen within PMNs) representing Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Ure.front: How is gonococcal distinguished from non-gonococcal urethritis on microscopy?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Ure.back: PMNs WITH Gram-negative intracellular diplococci = gonococcal urethritis; PMNs WITHOUT diplococci = non-gonococcal urethritis (treat empirically for chlamydia/M. genitalium, e.g. doxycycline).

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Ure.front: Why must a negative urethral smear never be used to exclude infection?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Ure.back: Microscopy is insensitive in asymptomatic patients and in female, pharyngeal and rectal infection. NAAT (plus culture for gonorrhoea) must always be sent regardless of the smear result.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Ure.front: What patient preparation improves the yield of a urethral smear?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Ure.back: The patient should ideally not have passed urine for at least 2 hours, so that discharge and PMNs are not washed out of the urethra before sampling.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.front: What is the key difference between treponemal and non-treponemal syphilis tests?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.back: Treponemal tests (EIA/CLIA screen, TPPA confirm) detect antibody specific to T. pallidum and stay positive for life (confirm exposure). Non-treponemal tests (RPR/VDRL) detect anti-cardiolipin antibody, are quantitative (titre) and reflect current disease activity, falling with successful treatment.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.front: What change in RPR/VDRL titre indicates successful treatment versus reinfection/failure?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.back: A ≥4-fold (2-dilution) FALL in titre indicates a successful treatment response. A ≥4-fold RISE indicates reinfection or treatment failure.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.front: How do you interpret treponemal positive + RPR negative?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.back: Suggests treated or late latent infection, or very early primary infection. Because treponemal tests remain positive for life, it must be interpreted alongside the clinical history and any prior results.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.front: What is the prozone phenomenon in syphilis serology?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.back: In very high-titre (often secondary) syphilis, antibody excess can inhibit agglutination and cause a FALSE-NEGATIVE RPR/VDRL. Diluting the serum restores a positive result.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.front: In what situations do biological false-positive non-treponemal tests occur, and what is the treatment for active syphilis?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.back:
Biological false positives (RPR/VDRL) occur in
  • pregnancy
  • autoimmune disease (e.g. antiphospholipid syndrome/SLE)
  • and other infections.
Active syphilis is treated with intramuscular benzathine penicillin.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.front: A treated syphilis patient shows a ≥4-fold RISE in RPR titre — what does it mean and what do you do?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.back: It indicates reinfection or treatment failure. Re-treat and reassess (take a sexual history for reinfection, and consider a lumbar puncture / CSF-VDRL to exclude neurosyphilis).

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.front: What reaction should you warn about when starting penicillin for syphilis?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.back: The Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction — fever, myalgia, headache and worsening rash within hours of the first dose, caused by release of treponemal antigens as organisms are killed. It is self-limiting; manage with antipyretics/supportive care (not an allergy).

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Dar.front: Why use dark-field microscopy or PCR rather than serology in suspected early primary syphilis?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Dar.back: They detect T. pallidum directly from lesion fluid, so they can confirm syphilis when serology is still negative because antibodies have not yet developed in very early primary infection.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Dar.front: What does dark-field microscopy actually visualise, and from what specimen?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Dar.back: The live, motile, corkscrew-shaped spirochaete itself, seen glowing against a black background in fresh serous exudate expressed from an early lesion (primary chancre or moist secondary lesion).

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Dar.front: Why is PCR preferred over dark-field microscopy for oral or rectal syphilitic lesions?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Dar.back: Commensal (non-pathogenic) treponemes at those sites are morphologically similar and cause false positives on dark-field. PCR targets T. pallidum-specific DNA, so it is specific and does not need live, motile organisms.

No. A negative direct test does not exclude the diagnosis; repeat the sampling and always send/repeat serology. Prior antibiotics or antiseptic and a dry or healing lesion can all cause false negatives.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Dar.front: What clinical ulcer description should prompt direct testing for syphilis?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Dar.back: A painless, indurated genital ulcer is a primary syphilitic chancre until proven otherwise, and should be sampled directly for dark-field microscopy or PCR.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Dar.front: A genital chancre is dark-field/PCR positive but serology is still negative — what is the next step?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Dar.back: Diagnose and treat primary syphilis now with IM benzathine penicillin. Direct detection is diagnostic in early primary syphilis, so treatment must not wait for serology to seroconvert. Syphilis ›

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HSV.front: What is HSV PCR used for in a patient with a genital ulcer?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HSV.back: To confirm herpes simplex virus as the cause and to TYPE the virus as HSV-1 or HSV-2, using a swab from the lesion base. Typing guides prognosis and counselling.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HSV.front: Why has PCR replaced viral culture for genital herpes?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HSV.back: PCR is far more sensitive, detecting HSV DNA even at low viral loads, and it gives rapid type-specific results (HSV-1 vs HSV-2).

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HSV.front: How should the swab be taken to maximise yield?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HSV.back: De-roof a vesicle and firmly swab the BASE of the fresh vesicle/ulcer. A dry, crusted or healing lesion sheds little virus and gives a lower yield.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HSV.front: What does detection of HSV-2 (vs HSV-1) imply?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HSV.back: HSV-2 recurs more frequently than HSV-1, so its detection prompts discussion of suppressive antiviral therapy.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HSV.front: Why is a primary genital herpes episode in the third trimester dangerous?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HSV.back: It risks neonatal herpes via vertical transmission. It warrants aciclovir and consideration of caesarean delivery.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HSV.front: Besides antivirals, what supportive care matters in a first (primary) episode of genital herpes?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HSV.back:
• Simple analgesia
  • saline (saltwater) bathing of the lesions
  • topical anaesthetic gel (e.g. lidocaine) for dysuria
  • and good fluid intake to avoid urinary retention — a recognised complication of a painful primary episode (may need catheterisation).

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Sca.front: What is the dermoscopic hallmark of a scabies burrow?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Sca.back: The delta-wing (jet-with-contrail) sign - a dark triangular structure representing the mite's head and mouthparts at the leading end of the burrow, resembling a jet aircraft with a contrail (the burrow).

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Sca.front: How is a scabies skin scraping prepared and what confirms the diagnosis?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Sca.back: A burrow is scraped with a scalpel blade onto a slide, mounted in KOH (or mineral oil) and examined microscopically. Finding a mite, eggs or faecal pellets (scybala) confirms scabies.

• Finger webs
  • flexor wrists
  • genitalia (penile/scrotal)
  • axillae
  • areolae
  • and the periumbilical region.
Itch is typically worse at night and often affects household contacts.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Sca.front: What is the first-line treatment for classical scabies?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Sca.back: Topical permethrin 5% cream to the whole body including scalp, neck, face and ears (and under the nails), washed off after 8-12 hours and repeated after 1 week. All close contacts are treated simultaneously and bedding/clothing washed hot.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Sca.front: What is crusted (Norwegian) scabies and how does its management differ?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Sca.back: A hyperkeratotic form in immunocompromised/elderly patients with an enormous mite burden that is extremely contagious. It requires isolation plus combined oral ivermectin and topical permethrin, and treatment of all contacts.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Sca.front: A patient treated for scabies still itches two weeks later — is this treatment failure, and how is it managed?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Sca.back: Usually no — post-scabetic itch (a delayed type-IV hypersensitivity) persists for 2–4 weeks after successful eradication. Manage with emollients, an antihistamine or a short course of a mild topical steroid; do not re-apply scabicide unless there is evidence of active reinfestation (new burrows/contacts).

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.front: For which STIs is a test of cure routinely indicated?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.back:
• Gonorrhoea (all cases, due to resistance)
  • Mycoplasma genitalium
  • syphilis (via serial RPR/VDRL titres)
  • and chlamydia in pregnancy.
Routine uncomplicated chlamydia in the non-pregnant does NOT need a TOC.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.front: Why must a NAAT-based test of cure not be done too early?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.back: NAATs detect nucleic acid regardless of organism viability. Residual dead DNA/RNA from killed organisms can produce a false-positive result if tested prematurely, so wait about 2-5 weeks after treatment.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.front: How is treatment response to syphilis monitored?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.back: By serial non-treponemal titres (RPR or VDRL). A fourfold (two-dilution) fall in titre confirms an adequate response to treatment.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.front: What is done for uncomplicated chlamydia instead of a test of cure?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.back: No routine TOC is required; instead a re-test (retest) at around 3 months is offered to detect reinfection rather than treatment failure.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.front: What are the two components of partner notification for a current partner?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.back: Trace, test and treat contacts within the relevant look-back period, and offer epidemiological (empirical) treatment to current partners without waiting for their results, while advising abstinence until all are treated.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.front: What should be offered to a notified sexual contact — just treatment for the index infection?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.back: No — offer a full STI screen (chlamydia/gonorrhoea NAAT, HIV and syphilis serology, hepatitis where indicated) PLUS epidemiological (empirical) treatment for the index infection. A contact of one STI is a contact of all.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.front: What safeguarding points arise in a sexual-health / partner-notification consultation?
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.back: Under-13s cannot consent to sexual activity (automatic safeguarding referral); assess Fraser competence in under-16s; and stay alert to coercion, exploitation or abuse, which contact tracing may surface. Confidentiality is maintained but is not absolute where a child or vulnerable adult is at risk.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HIV.question: A man has a possible HIV exposure and attends 10 days later requesting reassurance. His 4th-generation Ag/Ab assay is negative. What is the most appropriate advice?
options: The negative result reliably excludes HIV
No further testing is ever required after any negative result
Repeat the 4th-generation test at 45 days after exposure
Start lifelong antiretroviral therapy immediately
A CD4 count is the correct test to exclude infection
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HIV.answer: Repeat the 4th-generation test at 45 days after exposure
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HIV.explanation: A test at 10 days falls within the window period, so a negative result cannot exclude very recent infection. A 4th-generation assay repeated at 45 days after exposure is needed to reliably exclude HIV.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HIV.question: A patient with newly diagnosed HIV has a CD4 count of 150 cells/mm3. What does this value indicate?
options: Normal immune function requiring no action
That the person is not infected with HIV
That the viral load must be undetectable
That antiretroviral therapy should be stopped
An AIDS-defining threshold warranting opportunistic-infection prophylaxis
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HIV.answer: An AIDS-defining threshold warranting opportunistic-infection prophylaxis
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HIV.explanation: A CD4 count below 200 cells/mm3 defines AIDS-level immune risk with high susceptibility to opportunistic infection. Prophylaxis such as co-trimoxazole against PCP should be started.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HIV.question: A screening 4th-generation HIV assay returns a reactive result. What is the correct next step before informing the patient of a diagnosis?
options: Immediately confirm the diagnosis on this result alone
Perform a supplementary confirmatory assay
Measure the CD4 count to confirm infection
Start post-exposure prophylaxis
Repeat the same screening test in 3 months
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HIV.explanation: A reactive screening assay must be verified with a second, supplementary confirmatory assay before a diagnosis is made. This guards against false-positive screening results.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HIV.question: A patient has HIV confirmed on a supplementary assay; their CD4 count is 480 cells/mm3. What is the most appropriate management?
options: Withhold ART until the CD4 count falls below 350
Start ART only once the CD4 count is below 200
Give co-trimoxazole prophylaxis and defer ART
Refer to specialist care and start ART promptly regardless of CD4
Repeat the screening assay in 3 months before acting
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HIV.answer: Refer to specialist care and start ART promptly regardless of CD4
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HIV.explanation: UK/BHIVA practice is to offer ART to everyone with HIV at diagnosis, irrespective of CD4 count, aiming for viral suppression (undetectable = untransmittable). Opportunistic-infection prophylaxis is added only when CD4 <200; it does not replace ART.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__STI.question: A 22-year-old asymptomatic woman attends for opportunistic chlamydia screening. Which specimen gives the most sensitive NAAT result?
options: First-void urine
Endocervical culture
Self-taken vulvovaginal swab
Mid-stream urine
Serum antibody test
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__STI.explanation: In women the self-taken vulvovaginal swab is the most sensitive genital specimen for NAAT and is preferred over urine. NAAT detects pathogen nucleic acid with far greater sensitivity than culture.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__STI.question: A man who has sex with men reports receptive anal and oral intercourse. To avoid missing infection, testing should include:
options: First-void urine only
Vulvovaginal swab
Blood cultures
Urethral culture alone
First-void urine plus pharyngeal and rectal NAAT swabs
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__STI.answer: First-void urine plus pharyngeal and rectal NAAT swabs
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__STI.explanation: Genital-only testing misses extragenital infection, so pharyngeal and rectal swabs must be added according to the sexual history. Sampling every exposed site is essential to detect infection and interrupt transmission.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__STI.question: A patient's gonorrhoea NAAT is positive. What is the most appropriate next step before starting treatment?
options: Treat immediately with azithromycin alone
Take a culture to test antibiotic sensitivities
Repeat the NAAT in three months
Request serology for confirmation
Give empirical treatment without further testing
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__STI.answer: Take a culture to test antibiotic sensitivities
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__STI.explanation: A positive gonorrhoea NAAT should be backed by culture before treatment because NAAT provides no sensitivity data. Culture guides antibiotic choice, which is critical given rising gonococcal antimicrobial resistance.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__STI.question: A 24-year-old woman has a positive chlamydia NAAT on a vulvovaginal swab. What is the first-line treatment?
options: A single 1 g dose of azithromycin
IM ceftriaxone
Oral metronidazole
Doxycycline 100 mg BD for 7 days
No treatment unless symptomatic
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__STI.explanation: First-line treatment for uncomplicated chlamydia is doxycycline 100 mg BD for 7 days (it has displaced single-dose azithromycin, which is now reserved for when doxycycline is contraindicated or in pregnancy). Partner notification should also be arranged.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Gon.question: A man with urethral discharge has a positive gonorrhoea NAAT. What is the most important reason to also take a charcoal swab for culture before starting antibiotics?
options: To confirm the presence of gonococcal DNA
To screen simultaneously for chlamydia
To obtain antibiotic sensitivities given escalating resistance
To measure the patient's antibody titres
To assess the patient's white cell count
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Gon.answer: To obtain antibiotic sensitivities given escalating resistance
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Gon.explanation: NAAT confirms infection but cannot provide sensitivities. Because N. gonorrhoeae is increasingly resistant, a culture taken before treatment is essential to guide effective therapy and allow a test of cure.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Gon.question: What is the specific role of the charcoal in a charcoal transport swab used for gonorrhoea culture?
options: It amplifies the gonococcal DNA for detection
It stains the diplococci for microscopy
It provides antibiotic to suppress contaminants
It fixes the sample to prevent any bacterial growth
It neutralises toxic substances and preserves the fragile organism in transit
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Gon.answer: It neutralises toxic substances and preserves the fragile organism in transit
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Gon.explanation: N. gonorrhoeae is fastidious and delicate and dies quickly outside the body. The charcoal in Amies medium neutralises toxic metabolites, keeping the organism viable until it can be plated on selective media.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Gon.question: A patient is diagnosed with gonorrhoea and cultures confirm sensitivity. What is the recommended first-line treatment?
options: A 7-day course of oral doxycycline
A single intramuscular dose of ceftriaxone
A single oral dose of ciprofloxacin
Intravenous benzylpenicillin for 5 days
Topical chloramphenicol ointment
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Gon.answer: A single intramuscular dose of ceftriaxone
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Gon.explanation: First-line treatment for gonorrhoea is a single IM dose of ceftriaxone, tailored to sensitivities. A test of cure is arranged afterwards because of the risk of antimicrobial resistance.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Gon.question: A patient has a positive gonorrhoea NAAT but the charcoal-swab culture returns no growth. What is the correct interpretation?
options: The NAAT must be a false positive; do not treat
Repeat the NAAT in three months before acting
Only treat if symptoms are present
Treat for gonorrhoea anyway — culture is less sensitive than NAAT
Gonorrhoea is excluded by the negative culture
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Gon.answer: Treat for gonorrhoea anyway — culture is less sensitive than NAAT
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Gon.explanation: Culture is less sensitive than NAAT (and the organism is fragile, so a delayed or dry swab readily fails to grow). A negative culture alongside a positive NAAT does not exclude infection — treat for gonorrhoea; the culture is valuable for sensitivities, not for ruling out.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Ure.question: A 24-year-old man attends with purulent urethral discharge. A urethral Gram smear shows abundant polymorphs with Gram-negative intracellular diplococci. What is the presumptive diagnosis?
options: Gonococcal urethritis
Bacterial vaginosis
Chlamydial (non-gonococcal) urethritis
Candidal balanitis
Syphilitic chancre
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Ure.explanation: Gram-negative intracellular diplococci within polymorphs are the hallmark of Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Their presence alongside PMNs gives a presumptive diagnosis of gonococcal urethritis, and treatment for gonorrhoea should begin while culture and NAAT are pending.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Ure.question: A symptomatic man has a urethral smear showing increased polymorphs but no diplococci are seen. What is the most appropriate empirical management?
options: Reassure and give no treatment
Treat for chlamydia, e.g. with doxycycline
Treat only after NAAT results return in one week
Give a single dose of ceftriaxone for gonorrhoea
Prescribe topical antifungal cream
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Ure.answer: Treat for chlamydia, e.g. with doxycycline
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Ure.explanation: PMNs without diplococci indicate non-gonococcal urethritis, most often caused by Chlamydia trachomatis or Mycoplasma genitalium. Empirical treatment for chlamydia (typically doxycycline) is started at the same visit, with NAAT sent and partner notification offered.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Ure.question: Which statement about the sensitivity of urethral/genital Gram-stain microscopy is correct?
options: It reliably excludes gonorrhoea when negative
It is highly sensitive for pharyngeal and rectal gonorrhoea
It is insensitive in asymptomatic patients and at female, pharyngeal and rectal sites, so NAAT is still required
It replaces the need for culture in all patients
It is more sensitive than NAAT for chlamydia
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Ure.answer: It is insensitive in asymptomatic patients and at female, pharyngeal and rectal sites, so NAAT is still required
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Ure.explanation: Microscopy performs well in symptomatic men but is poor in asymptomatic infection and at female, pharyngeal and rectal sites. A negative smear cannot exclude infection, so a NAAT (and culture for gonorrhoea to guide sensitivities) must always be sent.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.question: A patient treated for syphilis 5 years ago is retested. Treponemal EIA/TPPA are positive but the RPR is non-reactive. How is this best interpreted?
options: Active untreated secondary syphilis requiring immediate treatment
A false-positive treponemal test that should be ignored
A previously treated (or latent) infection, since treponemal tests stay positive for life while RPR reflects activity
Definite neurosyphilis
Acute HIV seroconversion
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.answer: A previously treated (or latent) infection, since treponemal tests stay positive for life while RPR reflects activity
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.explanation: Treponemal tests remain reactive lifelong and simply confirm past exposure. A non-reactive RPR indicates absent or low current activity, consistent with prior treatment or latent disease when read with the history.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.question: A man treated for early syphilis had a baseline RPR of 1:32. Twelve months later his RPR is 1:2. What does this indicate?
options: Treatment failure requiring re-treatment
Reinfection with a new strain
A biological false positive
Development of tertiary syphilis
A successful treatment response (≥4-fold fall in titre)
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.answer: A successful treatment response (≥4-fold fall in titre)
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.explanation: A fall from 1:32 to 1:2 is a 4-dilution (16-fold) drop, well beyond the ≥4-fold threshold. A ≥4-fold fall in non-treponemal titre signifies a successful response to therapy.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.question: A patient with a florid secondary syphilis rash has a non-reactive RPR but a strongly positive treponemal test. What explains the negative RPR?
options: The patient does not have syphilis
The prozone phenomenon, corrected by diluting the serum
The treponemal test is falsely positive
Successful prior treatment
A laboratory contamination artefact
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.answer: The prozone phenomenon, corrected by diluting the serum
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.explanation: In high-titre secondary syphilis, antibody excess can inhibit agglutination and produce a false-negative RPR. Diluting the serum removes the excess and reveals a positive, appropriately high titre.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.question: Twelve months after treatment for syphilis, a patient’s RPR titre has risen from 1:4 to 1:32. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Reassure — this represents a treatment response
Repeat only the treponemal EIA
No action as treponemal tests stay positive for life
Re-treat and reassess for reinfection or treatment failure (consider LP)
Stop all follow-up
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.answer: Re-treat and reassess for reinfection or treatment failure (consider LP)
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Syp.explanation: A ≥4-fold rise in RPR titre (1:4 → 1:32 is a 3-dilution/8-fold rise) signals reinfection or treatment failure and prompts re-treatment plus reassessment — including a sexual history and consideration of a lumbar puncture to exclude neurosyphilis. A fall, not a rise, indicates response.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Dar.question: A 24-year-old man has a solitary painless, indurated genital ulcer of 5 days' duration. Syphilis serology is negative. What is the most appropriate next investigation to confirm the diagnosis?
options: Repeat serology in 3 months and take no further action now
Bacterial culture of the ulcer for Treponema pallidum
Dark-field microscopy or PCR of serous exudate from the ulcer
Gram stain of the ulcer exudate
Skin biopsy of the ulcer edge for histology
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Dar.answer: Dark-field microscopy or PCR of serous exudate from the ulcer
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Dar.explanation: In very early primary syphilis serology may be negative before antibodies develop, so direct detection from the lesion is required. Dark-field microscopy visualises the live motile spirochaete and PCR detects T. pallidum DNA directly from the chancre fluid.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Dar.question: A patient has a moist ulcerating lesion in the mouth and syphilis is suspected. Which direct test is most appropriate and why?
options: Dark-field microscopy, because oral lesions shed the most motile organisms
Dark-field microscopy, because PCR cannot detect T. pallidum at mucosal sites
Culture, because it distinguishes pathogenic from commensal treponemes
Neither, because oral lesions cannot be sampled for direct testing
PCR, because commensal oral treponemes cause false positives on dark-field microscopy
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Dar.answer: PCR, because commensal oral treponemes cause false positives on dark-field microscopy
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Dar.explanation: The oral cavity harbours non-pathogenic commensal spirochaetes that look like T. pallidum on dark-field, making microscopy unreliable there. PCR targets species-specific DNA, so it is the specific test of choice for oral and rectal lesions.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Dar.question: A dark-field examination of fluid from a genital ulcer is reported as negative. Serology is also negative. What is the correct interpretation?
options: Syphilis is confidently excluded and no follow-up is needed
Syphilis is not excluded; repeat sampling and repeat serology
The result is diagnostic of a non-syphilitic ulcer such as herpes
A positive result would have required culture confirmation anyway
Dark-field microscopy is only valid if performed on dried lesion crusts
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Dar.answer: Syphilis is not excluded; repeat sampling and repeat serology
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Dar.explanation: A negative direct test does not exclude syphilis, as too little exudate, prior antibiotics, or a healing lesion can all yield false negatives. The correct action is to repeat sampling and repeat serology over the following weeks.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Dar.question: A patient with a painless indurated genital ulcer has motile spirochaetes on dark-field microscopy, but the treponemal serology is (as yet) negative. What is the most appropriate management?
options: Withhold treatment until serology becomes positive
Repeat serology in 3 months and review
Start aciclovir for genital herpes
Treat for primary syphilis now with IM benzathine penicillin
Reassure — a negative serology excludes syphilis
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Dar.answer: Treat for primary syphilis now with IM benzathine penicillin
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Dar.explanation: A positive dark-field/PCR from a chancre is diagnostic of primary syphilis even before serology turns positive (direct detection precedes seroconversion). Treat now with IM benzathine penicillin; waiting for serology delays treatment of a confirmed infection.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HSV.question: A 24-year-old woman has painful grouped genital vesicles on an erythematous base. From where should the swab for HSV PCR be taken to maximise diagnostic yield?
options: The surface crust of a dry, healing lesion
The base of a de-roofed fresh vesicle
A clean area of adjacent normal skin
A high vaginal swab away from the lesion
The urethral meatus regardless of lesion site
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HSV.answer: The base of a de-roofed fresh vesicle
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HSV.explanation: The base of a fresh, de-roofed vesicle contains the highest viral load and infected epithelial cells. Swabbing here gives the most sensitive HSV PCR result.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HSV.question: HSV PCR on a genital ulcer swab returns positive for HSV-2. What is the main clinical implication compared with HSV-1?
options: It is untreatable with aciclovir
It excludes the possibility of recurrence
It indicates more frequent recurrences, so suppressive therapy may be discussed
It confirms coexisting syphilis
It means the lesion is non-infectious
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HSV.answer: It indicates more frequent recurrences, so suppressive therapy may be discussed
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HSV.explanation: HSV-2 recurs more often than HSV-1. Detecting HSV-2 therefore prompts a discussion about suppressive antiviral therapy for frequent recurrences.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HSV.question: A woman at 34 weeks' gestation presents with a painful FIRST episode of genital herpes confirmed on PCR. What is the key management concern?
options: Risk of neonatal herpes, warranting aciclovir and consideration of caesarean delivery
Immediate termination of pregnancy
No treatment as herpes is harmless in pregnancy
Urgent penicillin for the chancre
Reassurance that vaginal delivery carries no added risk
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HSV.answer: Risk of neonatal herpes, warranting aciclovir and consideration of caesarean delivery
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__HSV.explanation: A primary episode in the third trimester carries a high risk of vertical transmission and neonatal herpes. Management includes aciclovir and consideration of caesarean delivery to reduce transmission.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Sca.question: A 24-year-old man has widespread intensely itchy papules with itch worse at night; his flatmate is also itching. Dermoscopy of a finger-web lesion shows a dark triangular structure at the end of a linear track. What is this appearance called?
options: Auspitz sign
Wickham striae
Delta-wing (jet-with-contrail) sign
Nikolsky sign
Target lesion
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Sca.explanation: The dark triangle is the mite's head at the leading end of the burrow, with the burrow forming the contrail. This delta-wing sign on dermoscopy is diagnostic of scabies and confirms the clinical picture of nocturnal itch with an affected contact.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Sca.question: A burrow is scraped and mounted in potassium hydroxide (KOH) for microscopy. Which finding confirms a diagnosis of scabies?
options: Septate hyphae and spores
Gram-positive cocci in clusters
Multinucleated giant cells
Acid-fast bacilli
Mites, eggs or faecal pellets
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Sca.explanation: Microscopy of a scraping in KOH is confirmatory when it demonstrates the Sarcoptes mite, its oval eggs or faecal pellets (scybala). Septate hyphae indicate dermatophyte infection and multinucleated giant cells suggest herpes, not scabies.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Sca.question: An elderly nursing-home resident has thick hyperkeratotic crusted plaques teeming with mites and a ward outbreak of itch. Which management is most appropriate for this crusted (Norwegian) scabies?
options: A single application of topical hydrocortisone
Combined oral ivermectin plus topical permethrin with isolation
Oral antihistamine alone
Topical antifungal cream for 2 weeks
Reassurance and no contact treatment
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Sca.answer: Combined oral ivermectin plus topical permethrin with isolation
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Sca.explanation: Crusted scabies carries an enormous mite burden and is extremely contagious, so it requires isolation and combined oral ivermectin plus topical permethrin. All contacts must be treated simultaneously to control the institutional outbreak.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.question: A 24-year-old non-pregnant woman is treated for uncomplicated genital chlamydia and her symptoms resolve. What is the correct follow-up regarding a test of cure?
options: A NAAT test of cure 3 days after treatment
A NAAT test of cure 1 week after treatment
No routine test of cure; offer a re-test at around 3 months for reinfection
A culture-based test of cure at 2 weeks
Repeat serology at 6 weeks
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.answer: No routine test of cure; offer a re-test at around 3 months for reinfection
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.explanation: Routine uncomplicated chlamydia in the non-pregnant does not require a test of cure because treatment failure is uncommon. A re-test at about 3 months is offered instead to detect reinfection, which is the main ongoing risk.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.question: A man treated for gonorrhoea returns for follow-up. Why is a test of cure recommended in all cases of gonorrhoea?
options: Because gonorrhoea NAATs are highly inaccurate
Because gonorrhoea cannot be treated with antibiotics
Because a test of cure is legally mandatory for all STIs
Because symptoms always persist after successful treatment
Because rising antimicrobial resistance makes treatment failure a real risk
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.answer: Because rising antimicrobial resistance makes treatment failure a real risk
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.explanation: Gonorrhoea has developed widespread antimicrobial resistance, so eradication cannot be assumed after treatment. A test of cure (culture and/or NAAT) is recommended for everyone to confirm cure and detect resistant infection early.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.question: A patient asks why they should wait about 2-5 weeks before a NAAT test of cure rather than being tested a few days after finishing treatment. What is the best explanation?
options: Antibiotics interfere with the laboratory machine for several weeks
Residual non-viable nucleic acid can give a false-positive result if tested too early
NAATs only work once symptoms have fully resolved
The infection takes several weeks to become detectable
Early testing causes a false-negative from antibiotic residue
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.answer: Residual non-viable nucleic acid can give a false-positive result if tested too early
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.explanation: NAATs amplify nucleic acid whether or not the organism is alive, so dead DNA or RNA lingering after successful treatment can produce a false positive. Waiting about 2-5 weeks allows this residual material to clear so the result reflects true infection status.

investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.question: A man is contacted as the sexual partner of someone diagnosed with chlamydia. What should he be offered?
options: Only a chlamydia NAAT, with treatment if positive
Reassurance and no testing unless symptomatic
Treatment for chlamydia with no testing offered
A full STI screen (including HIV and syphilis serology) plus empirical treatment for chlamydia
A test of cure only
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.answer: A full STI screen (including HIV and syphilis serology) plus empirical treatment for chlamydia
investigations__SEXUAL HEALTH / GUM__Tes.explanation: A contact of one STI is a contact of all: offer a full sexual-health screen (chlamydia/gonorrhoea NAAT, HIV and syphilis serology) alongside epidemiological (empirical) treatment for the index infection (chlamydia). Testing for the index organism alone would miss co-infection.
